scenario: A clock move does the time-driven work at the next pump (RTIM.3.2.2): on the mock clock, a ttl-50ms fact asserted at 1 s, the clock advanced by 100 ms past its deadline, and the pump that follows retracts it, so working memory is empty after it. `temporal_sequence` reads working memory only after the last step ([RCTS.1.2.31]), the pump, so this pins the pump's retraction and nothing before it; that the fact is still present after the advance alone is RARC.7.15_an_advance_past_the_deadline_retracts_nothing's. Drives the libds and Mercury pump-entry TTL sweep through the runner's set / assert / advance / pump steps; it does not exercise a clock-mode switch.
